import Mathlib

open scoped IntermediateField
example {E F : Type*} [Field E] [Field F] [Algebra F E] (h : Module.finrank F E = 2) :
    ∃ x : E, F⟮x⟯ = ⊤ ∧
      (x ^ 2 ∈ Set.range (algebraMap F E) ∨
      CharP F 2 ∧ x ^ 2 - x ∈ Set.range (algebraMap F E)) := by
  have ns : ¬Function.Surjective (algebraMap F E) := fun hs =>
    Nat.one_lt_two.ne ((Module.finrank_of_bijective_algebraMap
      ⟨RingHom.injective (algebraMap F E), hs⟩).symm.trans h)
  unfold Function.Surjective at ns
  push Not at ns
  obtain ⟨b, hbF⟩ := ns
  have : Module.Finite F E := Classical.byContradiction fun nf =>
    two_ne_zero (h.symm.trans (Module.finrank_of_not_finite nf))
  have hbi : IsIntegral F b := .of_finite F b
  have hp : (minpoly F b).natDegree = 2 := by
    apply le_antisymm
    · rw [← h]
      apply minpoly.natDegree_le
    · apply le_of_not_gt
      intro hpd
      rw [← Finset.mem_Iio] at hpd
      generalize hd : (minpoly F b).natDegree = d at hpd
      fin_cases hpd
      · absurd minpoly.natDegree_pos hbi
        simp [hd]
      · obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := minpoly.natDegree_eq_one_iff.1 hd
        exact hbF c hc
  obtain ⟨u, v, huv⟩ : ∃ u v, minpoly F b = .X ^ 2 + .C u * .X + .C v := by
    refine ⟨(minpoly F b).coeff 1, (minpoly F b).coeff 0, ?_⟩
    rw [Polynomial.ext_iff_natDegree_le hp.le (by compute_degree!)]
    intro i hi
    interval_cases i
    · simp
    · simp
    · simp [hp ▸ (minpoly.monic hbi).coeff_natDegree]
  have hFb : F⟮b⟯ = ⊤ := by
    apply IntermediateField.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq
    · apply le_top
    · simp [h, IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank hbi, hp]
  by_cases hu : u = 0
  · refine ⟨b, hFb, .inl ⟨-v, ?_⟩⟩
    have h0 := minpoly.aeval F b
    rw [map_neg, neg_eq_iff_add_eq_zero, add_comm]
    rw [huv, hu] at h0
    simpa using h0
  by_cases h2 : CharP F 2
  · refine ⟨-b / algebraMap F E u, ?_, .inr ⟨h2, ⟨-v / u ^ 2, ?_⟩⟩⟩
    · rw [← top_le_iff, ← hFb, IntermediateField.adjoin_simple_le_iff]
      refine Eq.rec (motive := fun x _ => x ∈ _) ?_ ((mul_div_cancel₀ _ (mt
        (FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_eq_zero_iff F E).mp hu)).trans (neg_neg _))
      rw [neg_div, mul_neg]
      apply neg_mem
      apply mul_mem
      · apply algebraMap_mem
      · apply IntermediateField.mem_adjoin_simple_self
    · rw [map_div₀, map_neg, map_pow, neg_div, neg_div, neg_sq, div_pow,
        sub_neg_eq_add, neg_eq_iff_add_eq_zero, add_comm,
        ← zero_div (algebraMap F E u ^ 2), ← minpoly.aeval F b, huv]
      simp
      field
  · rw [Algebra.charP_iff F E] at h2
    have : (2 : E) ≠ 0 := fun h => h2
      (CharTwo.of_one_ne_zero_of_two_eq_zero one_ne_zero h)
    refine ⟨b + algebraMap F E u / 2, ?_, .inl ⟨u ^ 2 / 2 ^ 2 - v, ?_⟩⟩
    · rw [← top_le_iff, ← hFb, IntermediateField.adjoin_simple_le_iff]
      refine Eq.rec (motive := fun x _ => x ∈ _) ?_
        (add_sub_cancel_right b (algebraMap F E u / 2))
      apply sub_mem
      · apply IntermediateField.mem_adjoin_simple_self
      · apply div_mem
        · apply algebraMap_mem
        · simp
    · refine (eq_iff_eq_of_add_eq_add ?_).mp (minpoly.aeval F b)
      rw [huv, add_sq]
      simp [map_ofNat _ (nat_lit 2)]
      field

The general assertion underlying such a statement is essentially Kummer theory and Artin–Schreier theory (plus a bit of field theory / basic Galois theory). I would hope we eventually have all of this, but I guess we don't yet. In terms of the elementary assertion you wrote, what sort of assertion are you looking for to be in mathlib?
hopefully it would be stated in multiple different ways in order to be maximally easy to use (you could pick which one depending on what you want to do with it)

The case char ≠ 2 at least is kind of close to being in Mathlib in a "natural" way: (essentially it follows directly from docs#exists_root_adjoin_eq_top_of_isCyclic, docs#Algebra.IsQuadraticExtension.isGalois, and docs#Algebra.IsQuadraticExtension.isCyclic, after proving that any extension where the characteristic does not divide the degree is separable)

proof

import Mathlib

variable (F E : Type*) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E]

theorem Field.finInsepDegree_dvd :
    finInsepDegree F E ∣ Module.finrank F E := by
  simp [← finSepDegree_mul_finInsepDegree]

-- this is a pretty generally applicable formulation of this theorem
-- but probably not the most convenient one
theorem Algebra.IsSeparable.of_char_not_dvd_finrank (h : ¬ ringChar F ∣ Module.finrank F E) :
    Algebra.IsSeparable F E := by
  have _ : FiniteDimensional F E := .of_finrank_pos <| by contrapose! h; aesop
  obtain _ | ⟨p, hp, _⟩ := CharP.exists' F
  · infer_instance
  rw [ringChar.eq _ p] at h
  rw [isSeparable_iff_finInsepDegree_eq_one]
  have ⟨n, hn⟩ := finInsepDegree_eq_pow F E (ringExpChar F)
  obtain rfl : n = 0 := n.eq_zero_or_pos.resolve_right fun n_pos => by
    absurd h
    grw [← Field.finInsepDegree_dvd F E, hn, ringExpChar.eq _ p]
    exact p.div_pow_of_pos _ n_pos
  simp [hn]

@[simp] lemma primitiveRoots_two {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] :
    primitiveRoots 2 R = if ringChar R = 2 then ∅ else {-1} := by
  ext ζ
  have : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ 2 ↔ ζ = -1 ∧ ¬ ζ = 1 := by
    rw [IsPrimitiveRoot.iff_orderOf, orderOf_eq_prime_iff]
    aesop
  rw [mem_primitiveRoots (by simp), this]
  grind [neg_one_eq_one_iff]

open scoped IntermediateField in
example (h : Module.finrank F E = 2) (hE : ringChar F ≠ 2) :
    ∃ x : E, F⟮x⟯ = ⊤ ∧ x ^ 2 ∈ Set.range (algebraMap F E) := by
  have _ : Algebra.IsQuadraticExtension F E := { finrank_eq_two' := h }
  have _ : Algebra.IsSeparable F E := .of_char_not_dvd_finrank F E <| by
    obtain _ | ⟨p, hp, _⟩ := CharP.exists' F
    · simp [h]
    · rwa [h, Nat.prime_dvd_prime_iff_eq (ringChar.eq F p ▸ hp.out) Nat.prime_two]
  have ⟨α, hα2, hα⟩ := exists_root_adjoin_eq_top_of_isCyclic F E <| by simp [h, hE]
  exact ⟨α, hα, h ▸ hα2⟩

In char 2 the extension is either purely inseparable, in which case the primitive element theorem and docs#IsPurelyInseparable.pow_mem give another rapid proof, or separable, in which case it would follow immediately from Artin-Schreier theory (as Adam alluded to) but that's not in Mathlib yet afaict
(which could also be used to make my proof above a little shorter I guess, but the lemmata there seem useful)
